steps.description: Take the filtered blind vst matrix, select the 2000 genes with the highest variance across the 120 samples, and center each gene (median-center rows). Run ConsensusClusterPlus over k = 2..8 with 1000 resamples, 80% item (sample) subsampling and 80% feature subsampling, Pearson correlation distance and average linkage for hierarchical consensus, with an explicit random seed. steps.description: Take the chosen-k partition and the neighbouring-k partitions from T3S4 and test them three ways. (1) Stability: repeat the full clustering pipeline — gene selection, centering, clustering — on B >= 200 subsamples (80% of samples) and on bootstrap replicates, and score recovery of the reference partition by adjusted Rand index and by per-cluster Jaccard recovery; report the distribution, not just the mean. Also report silhouette widths on the consensus distance. (2) Null comparison: generate reference datasets with no true cluster structure that match the observed marginals — permute gene values within each gene across samples, and additionally simulate from a fitted negative-binomial / multivariate-normal-on-vst model with the observed per-gene means and variances but no group structure — run the identical pipeline, and compare the observed delta area, PAC, and ARI against the null distribution. State the empirical p-value or the explicit statement that the observed structure lies inside the null range. (3) Confounders: cross-tabulate the clusters against condition (case/control) with a chi-square or Fisher test, and against library size and detected-gene count with a Kruskal-Wallis test; report effect sizes, not only p-values. The step must conclude with one of: the data support k clusters beyond case/control; the data support only the case/control split; or no clustering is supported at all. Do not soften a null result.

plan.title: Blood cohort subgroup discovery beyond case/control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is class discovery: do the 120 whole-blood samples (60 case, 60 control; metadata.csv, 120 x 2) hold subgroups beyond the labelled case-vs-control split, how many, and how stable are they. The input is a gene-level Salmon count matrix (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 121 columns = gene id + 120 samples) whose length-correction state is not recorded, so the plan treats it as a raw count table, never rescales it before variance stabilisation, and records the import ambiguity as a caveat rather than assuming lengthScaledTPM.

T1S1 establishes sample structure on the variance-stabilised (blind) matrix: library sizes, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, coloured by condition. This is the honest first look at whether the dominant axis of variation is case/control at all, and it also produces the vst matrix every later step consumes. T1S2 applies filterByExpr so that low-count genes do not enter the variance ranking; with n=60 per group the filter is well determined. T3S4 is the core step: ConsensusClusterPlus over k = 2..8 with 1000 resamples, 80% item subsampling, on the top 2000 most variable genes after gene-wise centering, with Pearson distance and average linkage stated up front. k is chosen from the consensus CDF, the relative change in area under it, and confirmed by the proportion of ambiguous clustering (PAC) — the delta-area criterion alone reports structure in data that has none. T3S5 is the stability and confounder check that turns a partition into a claim or refuses to: bootstrap/subsample recovery of the chosen partition scored by adjusted Rand index, a null comparison against permuted or variance-matched simulated data, silhouette on the consensus distance, and a cross-tabulation of clusters against condition, library size, and detected-gene count. If clusters track library size, they are technical. If the observed PAC and ARI are not separated from the null, the answer to the research question is 'no subgroup structure beyond case/control is supported', and the plan says so rather than reporting a k anyway. T3S6 characterises whatever survives — limma-voom one-vs-rest marker genes per cluster and a whole-blood-plausible interpretation (cell-composition shifts are the leading alternative explanation for blood subclusters) — and is explicitly conditional on T3S5 supporting structure. T1S3 assembles the report with the reproducibility record.

No enrichment or differential case-vs-control testing is planned: the research question asks about sample structure, not about pathways or about the case/control contrast.

steps.method: blind VST + PCA + sample distance heatmap

parameters.name: clustering_report
parameters.value: input_transform, n_genes_kept, distance, linkage, n_resamples, k evidence, item consensus, cluster consensus, confounder table, null structure caution

(2) Null comparison: generate reference datasets with no true cluster structure that match the observed marginals — permute gene values within each gene across samples, and additionally simulate from a fitted negative-binomial / multivariate-normal-on-vst model with the observed per-gene means and variances but no group structure — run the identical pipeline, and compare the observed delta area, PAC, and ARI against the null distribution. State the empirical p-value or the explicit statement that the observed structure lies inside the null range. (3) Confounders: cross-tabulate the clusters against condition (case/control) with a chi-square or Fisher test, and against library size and detected-gene count with a Kruskal-Wallis test; report effect sizes, not only p-values. The step must conclude with one of: the data support k clusters beyond case/control; the data support only the case/control split; or no clustering is supported at all. Do not soften a null result.
steps.context: The metadata has no batch or processing columns, so library size and detected-gene count are the only technical variables available for the confounder table — say so, and note that unrecorded processing structure cannot be ruled out. In whole blood the leading biological alternative to a disease subgroup is a shift in leukocyte composition, which is not a technical artefact but is also not a disease subtype; flag it as the competing explanation to be tested in T3S6.
acceptance_criteria: ARI and per-cluster Jaccard recovery distributions across at least 200 resamples, reported for the chosen k and its neighbours
Silhouette widths per cluster on the consensus distance

Null comparison run with both a within-gene permutation null and a variance-matched simulated null, using the identical pipeline, with the observed delta area / PAC / ARI positioned against the null distribution
Cluster-by-condition contingency table with a test statistic and effect size
Cluster vs library size and cluster vs detected-gene count tested and reported
An explicit verdict: subgroups beyond case/control supported, only case/control supported, or no structure supported
Random seed recorded
constraints: Use the identical gene-selection, centering, distance, and linkage settings as T3S4 for every resample and every null replicate — a null run with different settings is not a null
Report the null comparison even when it contradicts the chosen k
Do not use a UMAP or t-SNE picture as evidence of separation
Report effect sizes alongside every p-value
caveats: A cluster that tracks library size or detected-gene count is a technical artefact and must be reported as such
With 120 samples and 12000 genes, subgroups smaller than roughly 10-15 samples will be poorly estimated; state the smallest cluster size and treat small clusters as unreliable
Cluster stability estimated on the same data that produced the clusters is optimistic; there is no external cohort here, so the estimate is internal only and must be labelled that way

grounding.reason: R-0141@ac9d requires the null-structure caution and a stability estimate before a cluster claim; R-0142@c982 requires the clusters be tabulated against condition, library size, and processing variables before any biological interpretation

steps.name: Characterisation of supported clusters
steps.question: If subgroup structure survives T3S5, which genes distinguish each cluster from the rest, and is the separating signal consistent with a shift in blood cell composition rather than a disease subgroup?
steps.description: Conditional on T3S5 concluding that structure beyond case/control is supported. Fit a limma-voom model on the filtered raw counts with TMM normalization and design ~ 0 + cluster (adding condition as a covariate where cluster and condition are not confounded), and test each cluster one-vs-rest. Report the top marker genes per cluster with log fold change and BH-adjusted p-values, and a heatmap of the top markers over the 120 samples annotated by cluster and condition. Then assess the leading alternative explanation for whole blood: score each sample for canonical leukocyte lineage marker sets (neutrophil, lymphocyte T/B, NK, monocyte, platelet, erythrocyte) using a simple mean-of-z-scores or singscore on the vst matrix, and test whether these scores differ across clusters. If they do, report the clusters as most consistent with a cell-composition axis and say so plainly. Also report the PCA loadings of the leading components as a descriptive gene-program summary, labelled as descriptive only. If T3S5 concluded no structure, this step instead produces a short negative report: the marker analysis is not run, and the reason is recorded.
steps.context: Marker genes derived from a contrast on the same samples that defined the clusters are circular by construction — the p-values are anticonservative and must be presented as descriptive characterisation, not as evidence that the clusters are real. The evidence that the clusters are real, or not, comes from T3S5. In whole blood, cell-composition variation reliably produces the largest transcriptome axis after any strong disease effect, which is why it is tested explicitly here rather than assumed away.
acceptance_criteria: Step is skipped with a written justification if T3S5 did not support structure beyond case/control
Per-cluster one-vs-rest marker tables with logFC and BH-adjusted p-values, explicitly labelled as circular/descriptive
Heatmap of top markers across all 120 samples annotated by cluster and condition
Leukocyte lineage signature scores per sample, compared across clusters with a test statistic and effect size
An explicit statement on whether the clusters are better explained by blood cell composition than by a disease subgroup
PCA loadings reported as descriptive only, with the note that a principal component is not a metagene
constraints: State prominently that the marker p-values are circular because the clusters were derived from the same expression matrix
Use TMM normalization inside limma-voom; do not pre-normalize the counts
If a cluster is nearly identical to the case or control label, say so and do not present its markers as novel subgroup biology

Lineage marker sets must be human whole-blood appropriate; if a curated cell-type marker resource is unavailable in the environment, use a small explicitly listed canonical marker set and state that it is hand-specified
caveats: No orthogonal measurement (flow cytometry, CBC) is available to confirm a composition explanation, so the composition assessment is transcriptome-internal and suggestive only

Deconvolution reference sets and gene set collections may or may not be provisioned; if a curated resource is absent, report the loss and fall back to the listed canonical markers rather than skipping the composition check

grounding.reason: No returned rule covers post-hoc characterisation of discovered clusters; drafted from standard practice, with the circularity of same-data marker testing stated in the step

steps.name: Clustering report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to whether the 120 blood samples hold subgroups beyond case versus control, how many, and how stable are they?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2, T3S4, T3S5, and T3S6. It must state: the input matrix and its transform (blind vst on Salmon gene counts of unknown length-correction state); the number of genes kept by filterByExpr and the top-2000 variance selection criterion; the distance (Pearson) and linkage (average) and the pam sensitivity run; the number of resamples (1000) and the subsample share (0.8); the evidence for k across k = 2..8 — consensus CDF, delta area, PAC; the per-sample cluster assignment with item consensus and the per-cluster cluster consensus; the cross-tabulation of clusters against condition, library size, and detected-gene count; the stability results (ARI, Jaccard, silhouette) and the null comparison; and the composition assessment. Close with a direct answer to the research question and the explicit statement that a clustering finds structure in random data, so any cluster reported here is a hypothesis awaiting an independent variable or an external cohort. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, every random seed, and the version of any gene set or annotation resource used.
steps.context: The audience needs a decision, not a gallery of consensus matrices. The report leads with the verdict — number of supported subgroups or none — and then shows the evidence that supports it, including the evidence that argues against it.
acceptance_criteria: Leads with a direct answer to the research question, including the case where the answer is 'no supported structure beyond case/control'
States input transform, genes kept, gene-selection criterion, distance, linkage, resample count, and subsample share
Reports the k evidence (consensus CDF, delta area, PAC) across all tested k
Includes the per-sample cluster table with item consensus and the per-cluster cluster consensus
Includes the cluster-by-condition, cluster-by-library-size, and cluster-by-detected-genes tables
Includes stability metrics and the null comparison, reported even where unfavourable
States the null-structure caution explicitly
Reproducibility record present: sessionInfo, package versions, all seeds, any collection or annotation version
constraints: report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release

report: clustering_report = input_transform, n_genes_kept, distance, linkage_or_partition, n_resamples, k_evidence_cdf_delta_area_pac, sample_cluster_with_item_consensus, cluster_consensus, cluster_confounder_table, null_structure_caution
Do not report a k as the answer if T3S5 placed the observed structure inside the null range
Do not present marker genes from T3S6 as independent confirmation of the clusters
caveats: The Salmon length-correction state of counts.csv is unrecorded; carry that limitation into the report rather than dropping it
There is no external validation cohort in this analysis, so every stability number is internal and optimistic
